title: Justify a principled refusal and its responsibilities

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: A principled refusal questions a demand and chooses a responsible method. Disobeying an internal club rule is not necessarily breaking law. Civil-disobedience analysis additionally examines stipulated legal status, public justification, alternatives, burden on others and accountability; conscience alone does not settle these.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Case A: a club requires an insulting initiation phrase. No legal requirement applies. A member may request a respectful alternative or decline membership. Case B is a fictional analysis only: a town law prohibits any peaceful gathering in its public square. A group proposes a public nonviolent breach against unequal access. A usable review process can answer within two days, the gathering is not urgent, and uninvolved users need an open passage. No action occurs.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Compare grounds, authority, alternatives and responsibilities in both cases. Apply the same reasoning to a group whose cause you dislike; do not design an actual breach.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: A conscientious refusal is private and breaches only a venue custom. Can an analyst call it legally prohibited civil disobedience without further facts?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: A permits bounded conscientious refusal without calling it lawbreaking. B does stipulate a legal breach, but the unused timely review and third-party access burden weaken a necessity justification. Its morality remains reasoned, not automatic. Partial: state a cause without examining methods. Incorrect: infer immunity from sincere belief or require surrender of legal rights. Real employment or legal disputes require their own facts and appropriate advice; this paper case authorizes none.
criteria: The authority and rule type are established
Methods and third-party burdens are examined
Conscience is not treated as automatic immunity

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: No. Preserve its conscience rationale while leaving legal status unknown. Identify what rule and authority would need establishing before making that description.
